title: TEMP — repo-ops build test on dcode-stack
instructions:
Work on the dcode-stack project in this workspace.

This is the whole project, not one file: it carries ten slices under `slices/`, each with
its own SPEC.md, plus docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. Read them as a set.

Follow your standing doctrine exactly:
  - If there is no project map, or the one that exists is stale, THIS RUN IS THE SURVEY.
    Find every spec markdown, read them, and write PROJECT_MAP.md at the repo root: each
    spec, what it requires, and whether the code satisfies it — built / partial / missing /
    drifted. Build nothing this run. A map is a finished run.
  - If a current map exists, pick the next gap it lists — the one that unblocks the most
    others — write the verifier first, and close that one gap.

Ground every status claim in something you actually read. "built" means you opened the code
and it does what the spec says, not that a file with the right name exists. Where a spec and
its implementation disagree, that is `drifted` and the disagreement is the finding.

Do not push, do not deploy, do not touch git history. Committing your own work is fine.
